title: 13th Sitting of Second session of 2026

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/13/2/2026).

Question by Maavashu MP Ahmed Shakir to the Minister of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development Dr Abdulla Muththalib: when will practical work on the L. Hithadhoo causeway begin, and when will it be completed?

Question by Kendhoo MP Mauroof Zakir to the Minister of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development Dr Abdulla Muththalib: the water and sewerage project in B. Fehendhoo and B. Fulhadhoo, on which the islands' whole economy depends, is about 60% complete and residents urgently need it; when will the work restart and when will it be finished?

Question by Maavashu MP Ahmed Shakir to the Minister of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development Dr Abdulla Muththalib: why has the L. Hithadhoo water and sewerage project stopped, when will it restart, and when will it be completed?

From the Speaker's desk: the President's nomination of a non-resident ambassador of the Maldives to the Kingdom of Bahrain, under Article 115(d) of the Constitution and Article 14 of the Foreign Service Act (Law No. 20/2021), is sent to the relevant standing committee for review.

Preliminary debate on the resolution submitted by Kendhoo MP Mauroof Zakir noting that, under the name of reducing staff at state-owned companies, many people are being dismissed from their jobs for political reasons, and seeking the views of Parliament's members on the matter.
Continuation of the debate on the bill to amend the Waste Management Act (Law No. 24/2022), submitted on behalf of the government by Ungoofaaru MP Ibrahim Shifaz.
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.

summary: The sitting put three questions to the infrastructure minister on Hithadhoo, Fehendhoo and Fulhadhoo projects, sent a Bahrain ambassador nomination to committee, opened debate on a resolution about political dismissals at state companies, and continued the Waste Management Act amendment debate.
